summary: Sends input CHOP channels as Open Sound Control messages to a configured network address and port.
key_concepts: OSC Out CHOP sends input CHOP channel names and values as Open Sound Control messages to a network address and port.
Protocol can use UDP messaging, multicast UDP messaging, or reliable messaging when the receiving workflow supports it.
Outgoing OSC messages are timestamped relative to the first outgoing frame's system time.
Send Events Every Cook controls whether all channels are emitted every cook or only changed channel values are sent.
Data Format selects current sample, current time slice, or transpose modes, and Transpose Name names transposed messages.
Max Bytes splits large OSC messages into smaller packets; use OSC Out DAT sendOSC() for explicit OSC bundle workflows.

key_params.name: protocol
key_params.note: UDP, multicast UDP, or reliable UDT messaging

key_params.name: cookalways
key_params.note: Cook and consider sending every frame

key_params.name: maxbytes
key_params.note: Maximum OSC packet size before splitting

key_params.name: sendevents
key_params.note: Send all channels every cook instead of only changed values

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: OSC CHOPs use UDP by default; messages are not guaranteed unless reliable messaging is explicitly used and supported.
By default behavior depends on Send Events Every Cook: either every cook or only changed channel values are sent.
Outgoing messages are timestamped relative to the first outgoing frame's system time.
OSC bundles are handled more flexibly by OSC Out DAT's sendOSC() when grouped/bundled messages are needed.
Channel names become OSC address/data identifiers, so generated channel naming must be intentional.
On Windows, firewall settings are a common cause of connection failures.
